# E0436: unsafe operation outside `unsafe`

Calling C, or reading through a pointer, can break every guarantee Stilt makes, so it stands inside `unsafe because "…" { … }`, whose reason says why the code is sound.

- Rule: [`c.unsafe-operations`](../../reference/20-builds.md#c.unsafe-operations)
- Reported at: the call, or the name of the function used as a value.
- Tier: `systems`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0436:6
use std.c

extern fn strlen(s: c.Str) -> u64

pub fn length(text: str) -> u64 {
  text.with_c_str(|s| strlen(s))
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
use std.c

extern fn strlen(s: c.Str) -> u64

pub fn length(text: str) -> u64 {
  unsafe because "with_c_str ends s with a NUL" { text.with_c_str(|s| strlen(s)) }
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0436_unsafe_operation_outside_unsafe.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0436_unsafe_operation_outside_unsafe.lt):

```text
── UNSAFE OPERATION OUTSIDE `unsafe` ── E0436_unsafe_operation_outside_unsafe.lt:6:23  [E0436]

This is an unsafe operation, which only an `unsafe because "…" { … }` block may
hold:

  6 │   text.with_c_str(|s| strlen(s))
    │                       ^^^^^^^^^

Calling C, or reading through a pointer, can break every guarantee Stilt makes,
so it stands inside `unsafe because "…" { … }`, whose reason says why the code
is sound.
```
